line: Good evening. I'm President Lena Ortiz. Tonight I'm asking Congress to clear the citizenship backlog, so families who have waited ten years stop waiting.
We will fund interpreters at every federally supported clinic. Nobody should leave a doctor's office not knowing what was said.
Our country has always been strongest when it lets people in and asks them to help build it.
To the people who keep two languages at the dinner table: you are not half of anything. You are the whole country.
Senator Lena Ortiz, on the Senate floor: "Reporting clinic visits to immigration agents will keep sick children at home. I will vote no."
This week I signed the language-access rule. Ask for an interpreter. It is your right now, not a favor.
Community centers, temples, mutual aid groups: you held people together when government didn't. We want to work with you, not around you.
Show up to your school board. Your library board. Your zoning meeting. That is where the country actually gets decided.
Ortiz again, at a podium: "...and I know not everyone agrees with me."
"...and we will keep working until it's done."
